Leduc et al. 2024 - plexDIA (Nat. Protoc.): monocyte, melanoma and PDAC cells

leduc2024_plexDIA.Rd

Single cell proteomics data acquired by the Slavov Lab. This is an update of leduc2022_plexDIA. The dataset contains quantitative information from three cell lines (U-937 monocyte, WM-989 Melanoma and CPAFII PDAC) at precursor, peptide and protein levels. This version of the data was acquired using the plexDIA MS acquisition protocol.

Format

A QFeatures object with 50 sets, each set being a SingleCellExperiment object:

  • Sets 1-47: log-transformed precursor-level single-cell data acquired using a 3-plex mTRAQ protocol, hence these assays contain 3 columns. Columns contain quantitative information from single cells or negative control samples.

  • peptides: peptide-level data containing quantitative data for 94080 peptides in 141 single cells.

  • proteins: protein-level data aggregated based on Protein.Ids, containing quantitative data for 8046 proteins in 141 single cells.

  • imported_proteins: protein-level table imported from the authors' protein report, containing 4619 proteins in 121 single cells.

The colData(leduc2024_plex_DIA()) contains cell type annotation and batch annotation that are common to all sets.

Source

The links to the data were found on the Slavov Lab website. The data were downloaded from the Google drive folder. The raw data and quantification data can also be found in the MassIVE repository MSV000093494: ftp://massive.ucsd.edu/MSV000093494.

Acquisition protocol

The data were acquired using the following setup. More information can be found in the source article (see References).

  • Cell isolation: CellenONE cell sorting.

  • Sample preparation: performed using the improved SCoPE2 protocol using the CellenONE liquid handling system: nPOP cell lysis (DMSO) + trypsin digestion + mTRAQ 3-plex labelling.

  • Separation: online nLC (NanoElute2) with a 25cm x 75um IonOpticks Aurora column and captive spray fitting (LC gradient 4-38% buffer B).

  • Mass spectrometry: timsTOF Ultra mass spectrometer.

  • Data analysis: DIA-NN.

Data collection

The PSM data were collected from a massIVE repository (see Source section). The folder f.MSV000093494/search contains the following file of interest:

  • report.tsv: PSM-level quantitative data

Sample metadata were collected from a shared Google Drive folder that is accessible from the SlavovLab website (see Source section). The folder contains the following files of interest:

  • plexDIA_SingleCell_Meta.csv: sample-level annotations

  • plexDIA_SingleCellxProtein.csv: processed protein-level data table provided by the authors, containing the imported_proteins data

We formatted sample-level annotations to ensure columns match with those of the quantification tables. Sample annotations containing NA values for neg samples were manually filled in based on the ID column in order to circumvent duplicate sample naming errors. These changes are incorporated in the file plexDIA_SingleCellxProtein_modified.csv, available on Zenodo.

Both quantification and annotation tables were then combined in a single QFeatures object using QFeatures::readQFeatures().

The script to reproduce the QFeatures object is available at inst/scripts/make-data_leduc2024_plexDIA.R.

References

Andrew Leduc, Luke Khoury, Joshua Cantlon, Saad Khan & Nikolai Slavov. 2024. “Massively parallel sample preparation for multiplexed single-cell proteomics using nPOP.” Nature Protocols 19: 3750–3776. Link to article.

Andrew Leduc, Gray Huffman, Joshua Cantlon, Saad Khan & Nikolai Slavov, 2022. “Exploring functional protein covariation across single cells using nPOP.” Genome Biology 23, 261. Link to article
